subject.title: Windows: lstat bottleneck causes 2-3x slower performance vs Mac (59% of CPU time)

question: Should OpenClaw accept operation-local realpath caches inside plugin hook/skill and sandbox containment checks for this Windows performance issue?
rationale: The original process-wide cache shape is too broad for security-sensitive path checks, while the linked scoped-cache PR still needs maintainer acceptance of the cache lifetime used around containment decisions.

options.title: Accept scoped caches after proof
options.body: Fix any remaining build/proof gaps in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85264, refresh Windows proof, and land the operation-local cache design.

options.title: Limit to non-containment caches
options.body: Do not cache containment-path realpaths, and treat the already merged manifest/plugin metadata cache work as the acceptable performance boundary.

options.title: Request a different design
options.body: Keep this issue open for an alternative that reduces Windows realpath churn without caching answers used by containment checks.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped caches after proof
recommendation.body: Fix any remaining build/proof gaps in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85264, refresh Windows proof, and land the operation-local cache design.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the fs-safe extraction and adjacent plugin realpath cache work, so he is the strongest routing candidate for the cache-lifetime/security-boundary choice.
